pipeline: Van Gogh Neural offline CV pipeline

source_image.note: Vincent van Gogh, The Starry Night (1889), MoMA

depth.convention: grayscale value 255 = nearest (village band), 0 = farthest (moon/stars). Raw model output preserved, min-max normalized.

flow.method: RAFT flow between the original painting and a synthetic next frame warped by a comprehensive displacement field: sky vortices at auto-detected luminous centers + two grand sky swirls + a horizontal band current + cypress sway + village and mountain drift, all region-weighted by the MobileSAM segmentation masks

encoding.flo: Middlebury float32, u then v per pixel, full resolution
encoding.rgb_png: R = u/(32)+0.5, G = v/(32)+0.5, B = |f|/16; value 128 = zero flow, clamped

layers.sky: complement of all other layers (masks partition the image, sum = 100%)

consumes.depth: uDepth -> pointer parallax + slow auto-drift (0.016 UV)
consumes.flow: uFlow (flow_raft_rgb.png, decode flow_px = (texel.rg - 0.5) * 32.0) -> per-layer phase-offset pulse advection, gain uFlowAmp=6.0; the v4 flow field itself carries per-region magnitudes (sky swirls/current ~7px, cypress sway / village / mountain drift ~3px each)
consumes.layers: six mask textures -> per-layer temporal phase (0/1.4/2.8/4.2/5.6/7.0 rad), procedural-wave regional weighting, star twinkle, village window flicker, moon glow breathing
consumes.guarantee: a procedural wave is blended on top of the neural flow so the whole canvas keeps moving even where RAFT underestimates

web_demo.fallback: if any asset fails to load, main.js degrades to the procedural wave shader (aspect-correct, clearly animated)

regeneration: see cv_pipeline/scripts/*.py (paths are machine-local; adapt SRC/OUT_DIR if re-running)
